interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology demonstrated a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT3a. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, no invasion of the seminal vesicles, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis, as stated in the surgical pathology report: "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3), pathological stage pT3a. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." This positive surgical margin and negative nodal status are reassuring factors. Countervailing findings are limited as nodal status was documented as negative. The prognosis is significantly influenced by the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, which are currently not recorded. Missing postoperative PSA data prevents assessment of biochemical recurrence. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory would be crucial in revising the prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 37.33 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 29.86–44.80 months; its coverage has not been validated.
